bugs.name: Disabled repository Packages page stays accessible
bugs.summary: After the repository Packages unit is disabled, its tab disappears and its direct URL still opens the Packages page.
bugs.expected: After the repository Packages unit is disabled and settings are saved, the repository Packages page should be unavailable through direct URL access as well as absent from navigation.
bugs.actual: The settings save succeeded and the Packages navigation item disappeared, but directly opening /eval/cu-packages-20260316-1537/packages loaded the Packages page with the visible empty state “There are no packages yet.”
reproSteps: At desktop viewport 1440×1000, use the supplied saved authentication state to sign in as the admin account; do not include or expose its saved-state path.
Open /repo/create and create a public repository owned by eval named cu-packages-20260316-1537, leaving unrelated settings at their defaults.

Open the new repository's Settings > Repository page, scroll to Advanced Settings, uncheck “Enable Repository Packages Registry,” and submit using the Update Settings button at the end of the Advanced Settings form.
Confirm the success notice and that Packages is absent from the repository navigation.
Navigate directly to /eval/cu-packages-20260316-1537/packages and observe the loaded Packages page and its empty-state message. Do not create or inspect package contents.
bugs.reason: Human review rejects the claim that hiding the repository Packages tab must also make its direct URL unavailable. Disabling this unit removes the tab but does not unpublish owner-owned packages or change their permissions. The repository listing still applies overall repository access checks and filters packages to that owner and repository. An administrator opening an empty listing establishes no failed supported task or unauthorized package access. The exact direct-URL behavior is consistent with this model; no explicit requirement for a 404 after disabling the unit was recovered.

bugs.name: Repository description is not displayed on the mobile repository page after creation
bugs.summary: A newly created empty private repository omits its entered description from the mobile repository page, including after refresh.
bugs.expected: The newly created repository page displays “Mobile repository description verification.”
bugs.actual: At 390×844, the created repository showed its name and Quick Guide, but not the entered description anywhere in the page. The omission remained after scrolling through the page and refreshing.
reproSteps: Sign in as fixture administrator eval and set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Create a uniquely named private repository owned by eval. Enter Mobile repository description verification as the description, leaving template and initialization unchecked.
Inspect the resulting empty repository homepage, scroll through its Quick Guide, and refresh. The entered description is absent from the visible page body.

As controls, open Repository Settings and the owner profile repository listing to confirm that the description was saved. After a first commit through New File, the normal repository homepage displays it at mobile and desktop widths.
bugs.reason: The user explicitly rejected this as intentional empty-repository presentation. The omission is real, but the saved description remains visible in Settings, the owner profile listing and the browser title; after the first commit, the repository homepage displays it normally. Empty repositories use a separate Quick Guide template. This records the human acceptance of that presentation, rather than claiming the original observation is false or that a maintainer explicitly required the omission. Desktop repetition alone does not invalidate the mobile observation.

bugs.name: Branch protection rule reports success but does not persist required approvals
bugs.summary: Saving Required approvals as 1 reports that the main branch protection rule was updated, but reopening it shows 0 again; this persisted across a second save attempt.
bugs.expected: After saving Required approvals as 1, reopening the main branch protection rule should show 1. The UI labels the setting Required approvals and says it limits merges to pull requests with enough approvals; the success banner says the rule was updated.
bugs.actual: The rule edit form showed 1 before saving and the page displayed “Branch protection for rule "main" has been updated.” Reopening Edit showed Required approvals as 0. Repeating the save and reopen produced the same result.
reproSteps: Using the provided authenticated session, start signed in as the admin account at /admin/harbor-handbook.

Open the top-navigation create menu (+) and choose New Repository. Create a fresh private repository owned by admin named management-branch-approval-qa-6d9c, with Initialize Repository checked so it has a README and main branch.
In the new repository, open Settings > Branches > Add New Rule.
Set Protected Branch Name Pattern to main, leave Required approvals at its default 0, then save the rule.
Click Edit for the main branch protection rule. Change Required approvals to 1 and click Save Rule.
Observe the success banner stating that branch protection for rule main has been updated. Reopen Edit for main and inspect Required approvals; it shows 0.
As a falsification check, set Required approvals to 1 and save once more, then reopen Edit for main. The success banner appears again, and Required approvals again shows 0.
bugs.reason: User-approved rejection after pinned-source review. The Required approvals form binds required_approvals, the handler assigns the submitted value directly, AllCols persists it, and reopening renders the stored value. The normal successful save of 1 does not silently persist 0 as claimed.
